key_concepts: Mixtures are physically combined substances that are not chemically combined
Suspensions are heterogeneous mixtures with particles large enough to be seen by the naked
Suspension particles settle when left undisturbed
Suspension particles scatter light through the Tyndall effect
Colloids are mixtures with solid or liquid particles dispersed uniformly throughout a gas,
Colloid particles are larger than molecules but smaller than what can be seen with the nak
Colloids appear homogeneous even though they are heterogeneous mixtures
Colloid particles do not settle in the dispersion medium
The Tyndall effect can be used to distinguish a true solution from a colloid
Types of colloids include sol, emulsion, foam, and aerosol
Common colloids include blood, whipped cream, fog, milk, gelatin, and mayonnaise
Colloids are used in food, medicines, cosmetics, and paints
